title: Find the circle's radius from points, then circumference
subtitle: Area and volume · 2 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **2 of the official questions in Area and volume are this one** — 0 Easy, 1 Medium, 1 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question shows points on a coordinate grid that 'define a circle' and asks for the circumference or area as kπ.
- No radius is given, so you have to find it from the positions of the points.

sections.heading: The method
body: - It is the point at the same distance from all the given points, often the midpoint of two points that sit opposite each other on the circle.
- 2) Count the distance from the centre to any one point to get r.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Then type (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r² with sliders for h, k and r, and adjust them until the circle passes through every point.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You may treat the distance between two opposite points (the diameter) as the radius, which doubles k.
Or you may give the diameter or r² when the question asks for the circumference.
